messages.subject: Multi-scale (Multi-method) detection histories
messages.subject_clean: Multi-scale (Multi-method) detection histories
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I would like to run a similar analysis to Nichols et al. 2008 and more recently Evans et al. 2019 where you account for the dependence between sampling devices at a site where you have more than 1 device. In my case, I have 2 cameras at each site that are separated to maximize my probability of detection at each site.

I would like to create a detection history that I can then use in RPresence (to my knowledge, you cannot implement multi-scale occupancy models in unmarked). As an example, if I have 2 cameras per site and 2 occasions then my detection history needs to be coded as: 01 00, where on occasion 1, the species was only detected by camera 2 and on occasion 2, the species was not detected by either camera. Currently, I have used the bycamera option to get rows for each camera for each site and occasions across the columns. I can probably figure out how to get the second camera into a row using some data wrangling, but curious if there is an option I am missing in CamTrap R to easily produce this.

Thanks in advance for any insight anyone might have.

Matt

messages.body_plain:
Hi Matt,
unfortunately, camtrapR doesn't have any functions or arguments that you could tweak to get the desired output out of the box. So as you said, for now you'd need to do some data wrangling to achieve the desired data format (after using detectionHistory with byCamera = TRUE).
And you are right, what camtrapR would support is setting byCamera = TRUE. You could then use camera-specific covariates to model differences in detection probabilities between cameras (if your cameras differ systematically, e.g. different camera models, or set up on different types of trails / roads).

Did anyone else miss this feature, input for multi-scale/method occupancy models?

Best regards,
Jürgen

messages.subject_clean: using the column with number of individuals to produce reports
messages.body_plain:
Dear group,

I am using the reports produced from "surveyReport" (CamtrapR, from an excel file with species, not from photos) to estimate the RAI´s (Relative abundance or capture freq) per species.  For this, I used "report_test[[5]]" which provides the number of events (n_events) per species needed. However, when doing the calculations I noticed that the number of events from the reports is the number of rows the species appears in the dataset, not the real number of individuals which we include in a separate column. Therefore using the rows will bias the results. So, I am wondering if there is a way to include this column of #of individuals to produce the reports. That would be one solution and would be great because anything containing the number of events could be used directly from the reports without bias.

Another solution that occurs to me would be to create new rows based on the values of the cell containing the number of individuals and repeat them as many times as needed (see below). Not sure if this is the best solution, though, since we have species that are found in groups of 10-40 individuals, so maybe not practical.

I would appreciate any feedback on this matter.

Thank you very much in advance.
Stay safe!
Lain

Generally, appendSpeciesNames() is done after identifying species in images (either via drag and drop or image metadata). You can also continue with your analyses without adding species names to images, as long as your images are identified.

messages.subject_clean: using the column with number of individuals to produce reports
messages.body_plain:
Hi Lain,
I think the simplest solution would be to create the desired output yourself directly from the record table. Something like this:

data("recordTableSample")

# add fake n_individual column for demonstration
recordTableSample$n_individual <- rpois(nrow(recordTableSample), 1) + 1

# sum up n_individual by station and species
out <- aggregate(recordTableSample$n_individual,
                 by = list(recordTableSample$Station,
                           recordTableSample$Species),
                 FUN = sum,
                 drop = TRUE)   # set to FALSE if needed (to match format of reportTest[[5]], but then also replace NA with 0)

# tidy up output
out <- out[order(out$Group.1, out$Group.2), ]
colnames(out) <- c("Station", "Species", "sum_individuals")
rownames(out) <- NULL

> head(out)
   Station Species sum_individuals
1 StationA     PBE               8
2 StationA     VTA               7
3 StationB     MNE               4
4 StationB     PBE              17
5 StationB     VTA               5
6 StationC     EGY              16

That would be the sum of individuals for each station and species. Is that what you were looking for?

You wrote:

> That would be one solution and would be great because anything containing the number of events could be used directly from the reports without bias.

I am a little confused here, because the current output (report_test[[5]]) gives the number of events already. Did you mean number of individuals?

Also, keep in mind that the same individuals may be recorded in different images. So simply summing up the number of individuals from all images of a species at a station will give misleading results and hugely overestimate true numbers of individuals.

Best regards and stay safe too,
Jürgen

So you assigned the species tags as, for example, "Species|Spotted_deer", not "Spotted_deer"?

Or would the tags in the example read "Species|Leopard Cat", "Species|Spotted_deer" etc? Also, when you use metadata tags, you can safely use spaces (Spotted deer instead of Spotted_deer).

But before you do anything, would you mind sharing a screenshot of your digiKam metadata tag tree please? Just to be sure I'm giving you the right advise. Or share a tagged sample image, then I can check the metadata.

Jürgen

messages.body_plain:
Dear Juergen,

Thank you very much for your quick response!
Yes, that´s what I was looking for. I need the format of report 5, since I need to create a  matrix of species per site. Many thanks!

That´s a valid concern that you raised. Most of the time the independent records (or events) have one single animal in the picture so not an issue. In rare occasions, we can have two animals in the same photo and very few other events (e.g. felids), not adding the individuals in that single photo could also underestimate the abundances, don´t you think?. But yes, it could also show more individuals than there actually are, especially for those social species that forage in groups for long time (antelopes in our case). We will have to set a criterium to balance this tradeoff depending on our questions and species involved in the analysis. The criteria of independence would help too. Maybe increasing the time frame for those very common or social species is better (more than 60 minutes or so), don´t you think? It is a bit of a tradeoff that we need to define after exploring our data set. Now, having being able to do it automatically will help us a lot.  I am curious though, would you recommend just ignore the number of individuals in the pictures as a "rule of thumb"? Thanks for your comment.

Best wishes,
Lain

messages.subject: camtrapR 2.0.0 on CRAN, including video support
messages.subject_clean: camtrapR 2.0.0 on CRAN, including video support
messages.body_plain:
Dear camtrapR users,

I am happy to announce the release of camtrapR 2.0.0 on CRAN, now featuring video support!

As usual, install it via:
install.packages("camtrapR")

In this version, recordTable() and recordTableIndividual() can process video files via a new argument "video". The workflow is identical to processing JPG images and supports identification via folder names and digiKam tags.

Due to video metadata being somewhat unreliable, there is no guarantee that it will work with any camera trap model. So first you need to confirm your cameras provide correct date and time in the video metadata.
You can use exifTagNames() to check if your video metadata contain a date/time tag (e.g. something like "QuickTime:CreateDate", not File Create / Access / Modify date). Make sure the value of the tag is identical to the time the video was taken. If a suitable date/time tag exists, Exiftool can extract it (analogous to extracting DateTimeOriginal from JPGs).
Furthermore, you can tag videos in digiKam, e.g. for species and individual identification or for assigning other information. camtrapR will then access the digiKam database to extract and tabulate those tags. But please be aware that (unlike JPGs) the video tags are not written into video metadata, so they are only present when the videos are in your digiKam database. They will be lost when videos are moved around or copied to other locations. Package "RSQLite" is required for this.

For more details on processing video files, please see the vignettes and function help files:

https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/camtrapR/vignettes/camtrapr1.html#video_support_(since_version_200)
https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/camtrapR/vignettes/camtrapr2.html#metadata_tagging   (find "And how about metadata extraction from videos?")

Note that currently video support is limited to two functions only. Moving forward, I am planning to enable video support in other functions of the workflow as well (imageRename, appendSpeciesNames, etc), but this will take some time to implement.

Besides video support, there is a number of other improvements in the new version, the most important ones being:
reliable creation of zip files in surveyReport() via package "zip"
improved output of exifTagNames()   [which now seems to make problems on Linux, please bear with me]
a set of sample images identified via metadata tags
improved error messages in many functions
prettier vignettes.
For a full list of changes and bugfixes, please see the package NEWS section <https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/camtrapR/news/news.html>

Video support is still in its early stages and somewhat experimental, so please let me know what you think, how it works for you, and how I can improve it for you.

If you test the video feature, would you please let me know:
what camera models did you use,
did it work,
what metadata tag did you use?
I can then provide information about what cameras are supported in the package documentation for future reference. Thank you very much!

One last thing, if you find camtrapR helpful and would like to support the development and support here in the Google Group, please consider making a donation to help me keep improving the package for you. See the welcome message on the Google Group main page <https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/camtrapr> for details, under "Donations". Thank you very much for your consideration.

All the best to you. Stay safe everyone!

Jürgen

messages.body_plain:
Hi Saloni,
I haven't encountered this issue before, and I believe it might have to do with your machine's locale settings, not digiKam or camtrapR.
Would you mind sharing the output of
sessionInfo() please?
Also, you can run exifTagNames() and share the line with "HierarchicalSubject". That is where camtrapR reads the species tage (and other tags) from, and if the accent is not there, then digiKam is innocent and it is somehow added in R. If in doubt, feel free to share some images (zipped to preserve metadata).

Alternatively, a quick workaround would be to just remove the character with gsub():

> x <- c("PantheraÁ tigris", "HyaenaÁ hyaena")
> gsub("Á", "", x)
[1] "Panthera tigris" "Hyaena hyaena"

Best regards,
Jürgen
